title: Prevent r901 supervisor Pulse from recursively scheduling itself
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `r901 supervisor pulse recursion` → no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: no related open/merged PR or issue found; recent routine scheduler work did not change the r901 definition.
- [x] File refs verified against current `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — coordinated scheduler definition, runtime guard, and regression tests.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped; production recovery should remain separate from the code fix.

## What

Prevent the externally scheduled r901 supervisor Pulse from being rediscovered
and synchronously executed by its own `evaluate_routines` stage. Represent r901
as externally managed and add a runtime self-recursion guard so stale generated
routine files cannot reintroduce the loop.

## Why

Production evidence repeatedly shows `routine r901 is due` followed by execution
of `scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`, while r901 remains at its old failed state and
later routines are not reached. The generated r901 description correctly says
launchd/systemd already schedules Pulse every two minutes, but the generated TODO
entry uses `repeat:cron(*/2 * * * *)`. Script routines execute synchronously, so
Pulse can wait on a nested Pulse invocation until the stage or parent is
terminated.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh:17-36` — change r901 from an
  evaluable cron entry to the existing externally managed `repeat:persistent`
  convention.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:291-295,365-379` — preserve persistent
  skipping and add a fail-safe that refuses to execute
  `scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` from routine evaluation, including stale generated
  TODO entries.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh:109-147` and
  `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-cron-extraction.sh:59-85` — keep
  generic cron parser coverage without encoding r901 as a Pulse-evaluated cron
  routine.
- Add or extend a focused routine evaluator regression test proving a stale
  r901 entry is skipped and a later due routine is still evaluated.

### Complete Write Surface

`get_core_routine_entries` writes generated personal routine TODO entries through
`init-routines-helper.sh`; `evaluate_routines` reads those entries and
`_routine_execute` synchronously invokes `run:` scripts. r901 descriptions and
platform schedulers remain launchd/systemd managed. Generated downstream routine
files must not be edited as the source fix.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Existing installations may retain a stale cron-form r901 until setup
  regenerates the routines repository, so the runtime guard is required in
  addition to changing the generator.
- Do not disable legitimate cron parsing or other core routines.
- Preserve direct launchd/systemd Pulse execution, explicit diagnostic
  invocations, and r901 tracking documentation.
- The guard must fail safe without advancing r901 successful state or blocking
  later routines.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-cron-extraction.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-calendar-scheduling.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh .agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh
```

Run the new or extended evaluator regression test separately and confirm it
observes both the negative self-execution guarantee and positive later-routine
execution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Generated r901 metadata uses the externally managed persistent convention
  while its description still reports the two-minute platform scheduler.
- [ ] `evaluate_routines` never invokes `pulse-wrapper.sh` through a routine TODO
  entry, even when the entry is stale and cron-form.
- [ ] A later due routine is evaluated in the same pass after stale r901 is
  skipped.
- [ ] Generic cron parsing, calendar scheduling, and ShellCheck remain clean.

title: Recover abandoned active rebase metadata in canonical mirrors
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: no prior lesson covered abandoned active rebase metadata.
- [x] Discovery: GH#28503/#28510 added recovery only for completed, converged stale rebases; no open issue or PR covers an abandoned active sequence.
- [x] File references verified against current `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — destructive-state recovery needs fail-closed invariants and race tests.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped; the recovery contract must be implemented and fixture-tested first.

## What

Add a separately confirmed, audited recovery operation for a clean canonical
checkout whose interactive rebase metadata is demonstrably abandoned but still
contains active todo entries or a stopped commit. Preserve the complete rebase
state and every referenced commit before clearing metadata without changing
HEAD, the index, or worktree content, then allow the existing default-branch
restore path to reconcile refs.

## Why

The existing `clear-stale-rebase` operation intentionally accepts only a
completed, converged sequence. A real canonical mirror is clean and has no
owning process, but retains months-old `rebase-merge` state with `msgnum=5`,
`end=10`, five todo entries, and `stopped-sha`. Later automation advanced HEAD
to the pinned remote tip while the local default ref remained one commit behind.
`clear-stale-rebase` correctly refuses this active-shaped state, while
`restore-default` cannot attach the branch until the abandoned metadata is
handled. This leaves no policy-compliant recovery route and blocks routine
enablement changes.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh` — add a distinct command and
  confirmation token for abandoned active rebase cleanup; do not weaken the
  converged `clear-stale-rebase` contract.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh` — add realistic
  active-sequence, race, dirty, divergent, and freshness fixtures.
- `.agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md` — document the new
  operator contract and the follow-up `restore-default` step.

### Required Safety Contract

- Require a clean worktree/index, no unmerged entries, structurally complete
  `rebase-merge` metadata for the configured default branch, and a distinct
  exact confirmation token.
- Pin `origin/<default>`, capture HEAD/local/remote refs and the index tree, and
  fail closed if any value or metadata fingerprint changes before cleanup.
- Require positive abandonment evidence rather than inferring it only from an
  active-shaped sequence. At minimum use an explicit age threshold and ensure
  HEAD no longer matches the stopped rebase commit; preserve conservative
  refusal for fresh or ambiguous state.
- Copy and verify every metadata file under the canonical recovery root and
  create durable recovery refs for HEAD, local/remote tips, and every commit ID
  referenced by todo/done/rewritten/stopped metadata before removal.
- Remove only the verified rebase metadata. Prove HEAD, local/remote refs,
  index tree, worktree status, and file content remain unchanged afterward.
- Keep `clear-stale-rebase` rejecting active todo/stopped state.
- Audit the authorization and preserved evidence without local/private paths in
  public output.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dedicated, exactly confirmed command recovers only demonstrably
  abandoned active rebase metadata.
- [ ] Complete metadata and all referenced commits are durably preserved before
  cleanup.
- [ ] The operation cannot change HEAD, refs, index, or worktree content.
- [ ] Fresh, dirty, divergent, malformed, concurrently changing, or ambiguous
  states fail closed without mutation.
- [ ] Existing converged cleanup behavior and tests remain unchanged.
- [ ] `restore-default` succeeds after an accepted abandoned-state cleanup.

## What

Generate Cloudron upstream-update issue titles from each package manifest's `title` field instead of the generic `Cloudron` label. For example, Buzz should produce `Buzz upstream v0.4.24 is available`.

## Why

The daily r916 monitor correctly detects and deduplicates upstream releases, but its hard-coded title makes findings ambiguous across package repositories. The current NetBird, AI DevOps Worker, and Buzz findings all exhibit the same generic title.

## Worker Guidance

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh` — capture the wrapper's `--title` argument and assert the manifest-specific title while preserving deduplication coverage.

### Reference Pattern

`_cloudron_monitor_upstream_entry()` already resolves `manifest_path`, reads `upstreamVersion`, and constructs the fingerprint, summary, and title. Keep the stable `upstream-v<version>` fingerprint unchanged so existing deduplication remains valid.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read `.title // empty` from the resolved manifest alongside `upstreamVersion`.
2. Fail with a clear package-specific error when the required title is empty.
3. Replace `Cloudron upstream v${latest_version} is available` with `${package_title} upstream v${latest_version} is available`.
4. Extend the focused fixture wrapper to record `--title` and assert `Example Package upstream v2.0.0 is available`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Do not mutate package manifests or release state.
- Preserve Bash 3.2 compatibility and explicit function returns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Missing or blank package titles fail closed with an actionable error.

- Focused tests and repository quality gates pass.

title: Review followup: PR #28157 — GH#28130: block merges on required human review threads
body:
<!-- aidevops:generator=review-followup source_pr=28157 fingerprint=source-pr-28157 -->
## Unaddressed review bot suggestions

PR #28157 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment
below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline
review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was
flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's
GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether
the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue
with a wontfix rationale.

**Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/28157

---

### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule)

This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched
directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false
premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without
measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `AGENTS.md`
"AI-Generated Issue Quality"). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting.

You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back
to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do
analysis.

#### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue

1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below).
2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that
   line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section
   isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a
   comment in this shape:

   > **Premise falsified.** \<what the bot claimed\>. \<what the code
   > actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>.
   > Not acting.

   No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next
   session reading this thread and the noise filter.

#### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR

1. Verify the bot's premise as above.
2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement.
3. Open a PR with `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in the body
   (use THIS issue's number, not the source PR's) so merge auto-closes it.
4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate,
   merge, postflight).

#### Outcome C — Premise correct but approach is a genuine judgment call

Only use this path if you reach it after Outcomes A and B don't apply:
the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is
architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside
what you can resolve autonomously. In that case, post a **decision
comment** with exactly these fields:

- **Premise check:** one line, confirming the finding is real.
- **Analysis:** 2-4 bullets on the trade-offs.
- **Recommended path:** the option you would take if the decision were
  yours, with rationale.
- **Specific question:** the single decision the human needs to make
  (yes/no or pick-one, not open-ended).

Then apply `needs-maintainer-review` and stop. The human wakes up to a
ready-to-approve recommendation, not a blank task.

> **Ambiguity about scope or style is not Outcome C.** Per
> `AGENTS.md` "Reasoning responsibility", the model does the
> thinking and delivers a recommendation. Only escalate what is genuinely
> a maintainer-only decision.

### Worker Guidance

**Files to modify:**

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:190`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:222`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:233`
- `.agents/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:88`

**Implementation steps (Outcome B path):**

1. Read the `diff` block under each inline comment below — it shows the
   exact code the bot was flagging. Open the file only if you need
   surrounding context beyond what the diff tail shows.

title: bug: gh-api-instrument.sh leaves orphaned .source.XXXXXX and .trim.XXXXXX tmpfiles on SIGKILL — up to 20 GB disk accumulation
body:
## Description

`gh-api-instrument.sh` creates two categories of temp files that are NOT cleaned up when the process is killed with `SIGKILL` (OOM killer, watchdog `kill -9`):

1. **`.source.XXXXXX`** — created by `gh_write_report()` at line 623: `snapshot=$(mktemp "${out}.source.XXXXXX")`. These are 128 MB snapshots of the raw gh API call log used as awk input. Cleanup exists at lines 629, 634, and 637 for normal exits, but no `trap EXIT/RETURN` handles SIGKILL.

2. **`.trim.XXXXXX`** — created by `gh_trim_log()` at line 663: `tmp=$(mktemp "${GH_API_LOG}.trim.XXXXXX")`. Cleanup at line 688 for the failure path; `mv` consumes the file on success. Same SIGKILL gap.

Both land in `~/.aidevops/logs/` alongside their respective base files.

## Observed Impact

159 orphaned `.source.XXXXXX` files discovered, each ~128 MB: **~20 GB total**.

Pulse runs `gh_write_report()` every cycle. If pulse is killed mid-snapshot (disk full → OOM, watchdog timeout, `systemd` restart), the snapshot is never removed. Over days the accumulation reaches tens of GB and triggers the disk-space dispatch gate (`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:2601`), blocking all new worker dispatches.

Circular effect: disk full → SIGKILL pulse → orphan snapshot → disk fuller → dispatch blocked → no workers to fix the cause.

## Reproducer

```
# After a watchdog kill or OOM event, observe:
ls -lh ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.*
# -rw------- 128M 2026-07-22 gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.JbOyxN
# -rw------- 129M 2026-07-22 gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.15Xu4J
# ... 159 files total, ~20 GB

ls -lh ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log.trim.*
# -rw------- 76M 2026-07-23 gh-api-calls.log.trim.HHHLmd
# -rw------- 49M 2026-07-21 gh-api-calls.log.trim.bC21y1
# -rw------- 30M 2026-07-23 gh-api-calls.log.trim.57nnCl
```

**Dispatch gate hit** (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`):
```
[dispatch_with_dedup] Dispatch blocked for #3119 in Majowka/mesh-manager:
  disk space critical (1949844KB avail on $HOME filesystem, need 5242880KB/5G).
  Run: worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged
```

**Causal code** (`gh-api-instrument.sh:623-637`):

```bash
snapshot=$(mktemp "${out}.source.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
chmod 0600 "$snapshot" 2>/dev/null || true
if ! _gh_snapshot_log "$snapshot"; then       # ← SIGKILL here → orphan
    rm -f "$tmp" "$snapshot"
    return 1
fi
if ! awk ... "$snapshot" >"$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then  # ← SIGKILL here → orphan
    rm -f "$tmp" "$snapshot"
    return 1
fi
rm -f "$snapshot"   # ← never reached on SIGKILL
```

**Causal code** (`gh-api-instrument.sh:663-689`):

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp "${GH_API_LOG}.trim.XXXXXX") || { _gh_log_lock_release; return 0; }
if LC_ALL=C awk ... "$GH_API_LOG" >"$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$GH_API_LOG"; then
    :
else
    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || true   # ← never reached on SIGKILL
fi
```

**Call-site sweep** (both functions sourced by pulse-wrapper.sh via shared gh wrappers):

```bash
rg "gh_write_report|gh_trim_log" .agents/scripts/ | grep -v test
# gh-api-instrument.sh: defined
# shared-gh-wrappers.sh: called after every pulse cycle
```

## Proposed Fix

**Option A — `trap` in subshell (handles SIGTERM/EXIT but not SIGKILL):**

```bash
gh_write_report() {
    ...
    local snapshot=""
    snapshot=$(mktemp "${out}.source.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
    trap 'rm -f "$snapshot" "$tmp"' RETURN  # cleans on any function exit
    ...
}
```

**Option B — Periodic stale-file cleanup (handles SIGKILL gap, recommended):**

Add to `pulse-cleanup.sh` or `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` preflight:

```bash
# Remove orphaned gh-api-instrument temp files older than 10 minutes
find "$HOME/.aidevops/logs/" -maxdepth 1 \
    \( -name "*.source.*" -o -name "*.trim.*" \) \
    -mmin +10 -type f -delete 2>/dev/null || true
```

Option B is the reliable fix for SIGKILL because Bash `trap` cannot catch `SIGKILL`. Option A additionally reduces orphans on graceful exits. Both together are the complete solution.

## Workarounds Applied

Manual: `find ~/.aidevops/logs/ -name "gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.*" -delete` freed ~20 GB. `find ~/.aidevops/logs/ -name "gh-api-calls.log.trim.*" -delete` freed ~155 MB. Dispatch resumed.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.172
- **Latest version**: 3.32.172
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

See-also: GH#28543 (disk-critical cleanup deadlock — related root cause chain).

The two issues compound: disk fills from orphaned tmpfiles → pulse killed → more orphaned tmpfiles → disk fuller → dispatch permanently blocked. GH#28543 addresses the worktree cleanup deadlock; this issue addresses the upstream accumulation that triggers it.

title: bug: review-thread-response worker exits without mark-complete or mark-blocked on positive-only bot threads — scanner retries indefinitely (attempt_count=31)
body:
## Description

When all unresolved review threads on a PR are **positive observations** from `github-actions` or similar bots (comments that approve a change rather than requesting a fix), the review-thread-response worker exits with exit 0 without calling either `scanner.sh mark-complete` or `scanner.sh mark-blocked`. This violates the worker contract v2 and causes the scanner to retry indefinitely.

The scanner's permanent-skip gate (`_should_dispatch():891`) requires `analysis_complete=true && maintainer_attention=true`. Since the worker never calls a scanner state command, `analysis_complete` remains `false`, and the scanner dispatches a new worker every cooldown cycle (3600s) forever.

## Root Cause

**Worker behavior gap (Bug A):** The worker prompt instructs workers to call `mark-complete` or `mark-blocked` at step 5. For positive-observation threads ("this change is correct and more specific"), workers interpret the situation as "no action needed from me" and exit without:
1. Calling `scanner.sh resolve <thread_id>` (which would clear the thread)
2. Calling `scanner.sh mark-complete` (which would set `analysis_complete=true`)

The prompt does not explicitly say: *"even if all threads are positive bot observations approving the PR, you MUST resolve each thread and then call mark-complete."*

**Scanner lack of fallback (Bug B):** `_should_dispatch()` has no upper bound on retries when `analysis_complete=false`. After `ESCALATE_AFTER` (3) attempts it sets `maintainer_attention=true` but still dispatches new workers indefinitely because `analysis_complete=false` prevents the permanent-skip at line 891.

## Observed Evidence

**State file for PR #3071 in Majowka/mesh-manager:**

```
attempt_count=31         ← 31 hourly retries, all futile
worker_contract_version=2  ← current contract, not a stale-version issue
maintainer_attention=true
attention_reason=same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint
analysis_complete        ← ABSENT (never set)
```

**Scanner log** (`pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log`):

```
[2026-07-24T06:04:04Z] dispatch: Majowka/mesh-manager#3071 not launching response worker
  — same unresolved thread fingerprint reached attempt 30;
    maintainer attention recommended (local state/log only, no GitHub write)
[2026-07-24T07:12:18Z] dispatch: ...attempt 31; maintainer attention recommended
```

Cycle: `dispatched=1` → worker exits 0 → fingerprint unchanged → cooldown → retry.

**Thread content (all 24 threads on PR #3071):**

All from `github-actions`, all positive:
```
"The original code caught a generic Exception. This change updates the test to
 expect SQLAlchemyError, which is more specific and informative. This aligns
 with the principle of catching specific exceptions."
```

No code changes requested. Worker sees these, decides "no action needed", exits without resolving or calling mark-complete.

**Manual resolution** (interactive session):

```bash
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh resolve Majowka/mesh-manager PRRT_kwDOPhWWNs6TCAEG
# → (no output, success)
```

All 24 threads resolved manually in ~5 minutes. Same pattern on PR #3097 (4 threads), #3104 (2), #3108 (17).

## Call-site Evidence

Permanent-skip gate (`pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:891`):

```bash
if [[ "$state_repeated_same_fingerprint" == true
   && "$analysis_complete" == true        # ← NEVER set (worker doesn't call mark-*)
   && "$maintainer_attention" == true ]]; then
    _prrts_log "skipped — analysis complete and blocked; maintainer attention pending"
    return 1  # permanent skip
fi
# Falls through to cooldown check → dispatches again
```

The `worker_contract_version` mismatch retry (line 852) does NOT fire because stored version (2) == current version (2). No stale contract issue.

## Proposed Fix

### Fix A — Worker prompt (primary)

Add explicit instruction for positive-observation threads. After the existing step 4 handling in the prompt template:

```markdown
4. For each unresolved bot finding:
   - If the thread is a positive observation (bot approving the PR's own change),
     verify the observation is accurate, then resolve immediately via
     `scanner.sh resolve`. Do not skip resolve for threads that require no code
     change — positive observations must still be resolved to satisfy branch
     protection.
```

And make step 5 unconditional:

```markdown
5. After completing the bounded pass, you MUST call one of these regardless of
   outcome:
   - All actionable threads resolved: mark-complete
   - Any thread intentionally left unresolved: mark-blocked
   Exiting without calling either is a contract violation that causes indefinite
   retry loops.
```

### Fix B — Scanner fallback (defense-in-depth)

Add an absolute retry cap in `_should_dispatch()` after the existing `maintainer_attention` + `analysis_complete` gate:

```bash
# New: stop dispatching when attempt_count far exceeds ESCALATE_AFTER
# regardless of analysis_complete — catches workers that exit without
# calling mark-complete or mark-blocked.
local absolute_cap=$(( PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_ESCALATE_AFTER * 5 ))
if [[ "$next_attempt_count" -gt "$absolute_cap" &&
      "$state_repeated_same_fingerprint" == true &&
      "$state_same_head_sha" == true ]]; then
    _prrts_log "dispatch: ${repo_slug}#${pr_number} skipped — exceeded absolute retry cap (${next_attempt_count}/${absolute_cap}); worker contract v${PRRTS_WORKER_CONTRACT_VERSION} did not call mark-complete or mark-blocked"
    return 1
fi
```

## Workarounds Applied

Manually resolved all 44 threads across PRs #3071, #3097, #3104, #3108 using `scanner.sh resolve` in an interactive session. PRs unblocked and proceeding to merge.

## Relationship to Prior Issues

- **GH#26124** (closed): addressed the case where workers CORRECTLY determine a thread needs maintainer attention but don't signal it. Fixed by adding `mark-blocked`. This issue is the inverse: workers exit without calling ANY state command even when the resolution path is clear (positive observations → resolve → mark-complete).

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.172
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

title: bug: worker-progress-blockers.jsonl never cleared for closed/not-planned issues — blocking=true persists forever, active blocker count inflated
body:
## Description

`worker-progress-blockers.jsonl` is an append-only log. Entries are written with `blocking: true` when a worker pauses for permission approval. The only path that writes `blocking: false` is `config-hook.mjs:355` — when a maintainer explicitly grants the permission and the worker resumes.

There is no path that writes `blocking: false` when:
1. The linked issue is closed or marked `not-planned`
2. The worker session exits for any reason without a grant
3. `sweep_closed_auto_dispatch_issues()` runs

**Result**: blocker records for closed issues accumulate permanently. `worker-activity-helper.sh` computes "active" blockers as the most recent event per identity with `blocking: true`. Once written, these records are never superseded.

## Observed Evidence

`worker-activity-helper.sh summary` reports `Currently active: 36`. Inspection of the actual issues:

| Session key | Issue | GitHub state | Blocker label | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `issue-3017` | #3017 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-2920` | #2920 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-1214` | #1214 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-2949` | #2949 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | none | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-3088` | #3088 Majowka/mesh-manager | OPEN | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | ✅ legitimate |
| `issue-40` | #40 Majowka/aidevops-routines | OPEN | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | ✅ legitimate |

At least 4 of 6 visible "active" blockers are zombie records for closed issues. The 36 total likely contains many more.

## Causal Code

**`worker-blocker-log.mjs:83`** — default `blocking: true`:
```javascript
blocking: input.blocking !== false,  // only false when caller explicitly passes blocking:false
```

**`config-hook.mjs:354-355`** — the ONLY path writing `blocking: false`:
```javascript
recordPermissionGrantEvent({
    event: "permission_grant_applied",
    status: "resuming", reason: "scoped_permission_granted",
    blocking: false,   // ← only on successful grant
});
```

**`worker-activity-helper.sh:347`** — active = last event per identity with `blocking: true`:
```javascript
($all | group_by(identity) | map(sort_by(.ts // 0) | last)
      | map(select(.blocking == true))) as $active
```

**`shared-dispatch-label-cleanup.sh:123-130`** — `sweep_closed_auto_dispatch_issues()` strips GitHub labels only, never writes blocker events:
```bash
gh issue list --repo "$repo_slug" --state closed --label "auto-dispatch" ...
clear_terminal_issue_dispatch_labels "$issue_number" ...
# ← no appendWorkerBlockerEvent call here
```

## Proposed Fix

### Fix A — sweep writes unblock events (primary)

In `sweep_closed_auto_dispatch_issues()`, after clearing labels, write `blocking: false` events for any active blocker records matching the closed issue:

```bash
# After clear_terminal_issue_dispatch_labels:
node "${SCRIPT_DIR}/worker-blocker-log.mjs" append \
    --issue "$issue_number" --repo "$repo_slug" \
    --event "issue_closed_sweep" --status "resolved" \
    --reason "issue_closed_not_planned" --blocking false
```

### Fix B — worker-activity-helper cross-checks GitHub state (defense-in-depth)

When computing active blockers, skip identities where the linked issue is confirmed closed:

```javascript
# In _wah_blocker_json: filter $active against a small gh api batch
# to verify issue state — or at minimum add a TTL (e.g. 30 days)
```

### Fix C — TTL on blockers (simplest short-term)

Add a max age to "active" computation in `worker-activity-helper.sh`. Records older than 30 days are never counted as active regardless of `blocking` field.

## Workarounds Applied

None — the zombie records are cosmetic (inflated count, misleading diagnostics) but do not directly block dispatch. Legitimate blockers (#3088, #40) are still visible among the noise.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.172
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

title: Trust boundary: external PR task-prefix titles bypass linkage and triage gates
body:
## What

Prevent external pull-request authors from using a spoofed `tNNN:` or `GH#NNN:` title prefix to bypass linked-issue, maintainer-triage, and bounty-spam policy gates.

PR #28237 demonstrated the gap: its author association is `CONTRIBUTOR`, its title starts with `GH#1214:`, `closingIssuesReferences` is empty, and the same-repository issue #1214 is unrelated. Despite that, the title alone produced successful/bypassed policy outcomes.

This repeats the trust-ordering defect fixed for issues by #20816 / #20832. A title is untrusted PR input and must never establish author trust or prove issue linkage.

## Why

Three workflow paths currently treat a task-shaped title as an internal provenance signal before validating the author:

- `.github/workflows/linked-issue-check.yml:94-99` returns success for any matching title without checking `author_association` or a real repository issue reference.
- `.github/workflows/pr-triage-gate.yml:47-58` returns before the `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` trust check, so an external author can evade `needs-maintainer-review` triage.
- `.github/workflows/bounty-spam-auto-close.yml:21-27,75-80` skips its external-author detector when the title has a task prefix.

The merge/review layers retain some defence in depth, but these bypasses weaken independent trust gates and make policy status misleading.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.github/workflows/linked-issue-check.yml` — permit title-prefix exemption only after immutable author-association trust is established; untrusted authors must provide a valid body issue reference.
- **EDIT:** `.github/workflows/pr-triage-gate.yml` — remove the title-prefix early returns; bot and trusted-role checks already cover legitimate internal authors.
- **EDIT:** `.github/workflows/bounty-spam-auto-close.yml` — remove title-prefix skip clauses and update the documented skip conditions; the job is already restricted to non-bot, non-trusted authors.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-linked-issue-guidance.sh` and/or a focused new workflow-policy test — cover trusted and untrusted title-prefix cases across all three workflows.

### Reference pattern

- Follow #20832: bot exemption first, then immutable `author_association` trust, then normal policy evaluation.
- Preserve GH#17671 defence in depth and add `#aidevops:trust-boundary` immediately above each new/reordered trust check.
- Do not infer trust from title/body text, labels writable by untrusted automation, or prior contribution status (`CONTRIBUTOR` remains untrusted).

### Implementation steps

1. Reorder or remove title-prefix exemptions so they cannot run for `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` authors.
2. Preserve bot and `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` behavior where each workflow intentionally exempts those identities.
3. Ensure an external title prefix does not count as linked-issue evidence; require the existing body-reference path instead.
4. Remove the redundant title skip from the external-only bounty detector.
5. Add regression coverage for both `tNNN:` and `GH#NNN:` titles, including trusted-author controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `CONTRIBUTOR` PR titled `t1234: ...` with no valid body reference fails the linked-issue policy.
- [ ] A `CONTRIBUTOR` PR titled `GH#1234: ...` with no valid body reference fails the linked-issue policy.
- [ ] Those same untrusted titles do not bypass `needs-maintainer-review` triage.
- [ ] Those same untrusted titles are still evaluated by the bounty-spam detector.
- [ ] Bot and `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` exemptions remain intentional and tested.
- [ ] New or reordered trust checks carry `#aidevops:trust-boundary` markers.
- [ ] Existing linked-issue and bounty detector tests pass.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-linked-issue-guidance.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-bounty-spam-detector.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh
```

Also inspect the workflow diff to confirm no external-author path can return/skip solely because a title matches `tNNN` or `GH#NNN`.

## Constraints

- Keep the change fail-closed for untrusted authors.
- Do not weaken the separate maintainer gate, review gate, or linked-issue body-reference validation.
- Do not special-case PR #28237 or any external repository reference.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — the edit surface is small, but it changes three security-sensitive GitHub trust gates and requires cross-workflow regression reasoning.

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Description

`gh-api-instrument.sh` creates two categories of temp files that are NOT cleaned up when the process is killed with `SIGKILL` (OOM killer, watchdog `kill -9`):

1. **`.source.XXXXXX`** — created by `gh_write_report()` at line 623: `snapshot=$(mktemp "${out}.source.XXXXXX")`. These are 128 MB snapshots of the raw gh API call log used as awk input. Cleanup exists at lines 629, 634, and 637 for normal exits, but no `trap EXIT/RETURN` handles SIGKILL.

2. **`.trim.XXXXXX`** — created by `gh_trim_log()` at line 663: `tmp=$(mktemp "${GH_API_LOG}.trim.XXXXXX")`. Cleanup at line 688 for the failure path; `mv` consumes the file on success. Same SIGKILL gap.

Both land in `~/.aidevops/logs/` alongside their respective base files.

## Observed Impact

159 orphaned `.source.XXXXXX` files discovered, each ~128 MB: **~20 GB total**.

Pulse runs `gh_write_report()` every cycle. If pulse is killed mid-snapshot (disk full → OOM, watchdog timeout, `systemd` restart), the snapshot is never removed. Over days the accumulation reaches tens of GB and triggers the disk-space dispatch gate (`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:2601`), blocking all new worker dispatches.

Circular effect: disk full → SIGKILL pulse → orphan snapshot → disk fuller → dispatch blocked → no workers to fix the cause.

## Reproducer

```
# After a watchdog kill or OOM event, observe:
ls -lh ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.*
# -rw------- 128M 2026-07-22 gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.JbOyxN
# -rw------- 129M 2026-07-22 gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.15Xu4J
# ... 159 files total, ~20 GB

ls -lh ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log.trim.*
# -rw------- 76M 2026-07-23 gh-api-calls.log.trim.HHHLmd
# -rw------- 49M 2026-07-21 gh-api-calls.log.trim.bC21y1
# -rw------- 30M 2026-07-23 gh-api-calls.log.trim.57nnCl
```

**Dispatch gate hit** (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`):
```
[dispatch_with_dedup] Dispatch blocked for #3119 in Majowka/mesh-manager:
  disk space critical (1949844KB avail on $HOME filesystem, need 5242880KB/5G).
  Run: worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged
```

**Causal code** (`gh-api-instrument.sh:623-637`):

```bash
snapshot=$(mktemp "${out}.source.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
chmod 0600 "$snapshot" 2>/dev/null || true
if ! _gh_snapshot_log "$snapshot"; then       # ← SIGKILL here → orphan
    rm -f "$tmp" "$snapshot"
    return 1
fi
if ! awk ... "$snapshot" >"$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then  # ← SIGKILL here → orphan
    rm -f "$tmp" "$snapshot"
    return 1
fi
rm -f "$snapshot"   # ← never reached on SIGKILL
```

**Causal code** (`gh-api-instrument.sh:663-689`):

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp "${GH_API_LOG}.trim.XXXXXX") || { _gh_log_lock_release; return 0; }
if LC_ALL=C awk ... "$GH_API_LOG" >"$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$GH_API_LOG"; then
    :
else
    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || true   # ← never reached on SIGKILL
fi
```

**Call-site sweep** (both functions sourced by pulse-wrapper.sh via shared gh wrappers):

```bash
rg "gh_write_report|gh_trim_log" .agents/scripts/ | grep -v test
# gh-api-instrument.sh: defined
# shared-gh-wrappers.sh: called after every pulse cycle
```

## Proposed Fix

**Option A — `trap` in subshell (handles SIGTERM/EXIT but not SIGKILL):**

```bash
gh_write_report() {
    ...
    local snapshot=""
    snapshot=$(mktemp "${out}.source.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
    trap 'rm -f "$snapshot" "$tmp"' RETURN  # cleans on any function exit
    ...
}
```

**Option B — Periodic stale-file cleanup (handles SIGKILL gap, recommended):**

Add to `pulse-cleanup.sh` or `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` preflight:

```bash
# Remove orphaned gh-api-instrument temp files older than 10 minutes
find "$HOME/.aidevops/logs/" -maxdepth 1 \
    \( -name "*.source.*" -o -name "*.trim.*" \) \
    -mmin +10 -type f -delete 2>/dev/null || true
```

Option B is the reliable fix for SIGKILL because Bash `trap` cannot catch `SIGKILL`. Option A additionally reduces orphans on graceful exits. Both together are the complete solution.

## Workarounds Applied

Manual: `find ~/.aidevops/logs/ -name "gh-api-calls-by-stage.json.source.*" -delete` freed ~20 GB. `find ~/.aidevops/logs/ -name "gh-api-calls.log.trim.*" -delete` freed ~155 MB. Dispatch resumed.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.172
- **Latest version**: 3.32.172
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

See-also: GH#28543 (disk-critical cleanup deadlock — related root cause chain).

The two issues compound: disk fills from orphaned tmpfiles → pulse killed → more orphaned tmpfiles → disk fuller → dispatch permanently blocked. GH#28543 addresses the worktree cleanup deadlock; this issue addresses the upstream accumulation that triggers it.

### Pre-Review Context

| Actual bug | Yes | Repeated full-log snapshots can remain permanently and consume enough disk to trip dispatch capacity checks. |
| In scope | Yes | This is reliability and lifecycle management for framework-owned telemetry scratch data. |

**Root Cause:** `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh` creates randomly named scratch files beside durable logs without durable owner identity or a later dead-owner reaper. Immediate cleanup handles ordinary exits, but no Bash trap can handle SIGKILL.

### Resolution Plan

Implement the minimal fix in `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`:

1. Allocate aggregate, trim, and report scratch files under a private managed directory derived from `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`.
2. Include the creator PID in each exact framework-owned filename.
3. Before allocation, remove only regular, non-symlink scratch files whose parsed owner PID is no longer alive.
4. Add one conservative migration sweep for the exact legacy telemetry scratch basenames.
5. Preserve immediate cleanup, locking, atomic report publication, 0600 files, and fail-open instrumentation.

Do **not** use a broad `find` deletion: it can delete unrelated or live files and races with long-running aggregation. Do not treat `RETURN` or `EXIT` traps as the SIGKILL fix. Avoiding snapshots is a separate, higher-churn redesign and is not required here.

| Safety gates touched | No approval, sandbox, prompt, privacy, review, or origin-label gate changes. Dispatch availability is indirectly improved; filesystem ownership and symlink invariants must remain fail-closed. |
| Symptom vs root cause | Root cause: gives abandoned scratch files a recoverable ownership lifecycle rather than raising disk thresholds. |
| Ripple effects | Scratch paths, telemetry aggregation and trim concurrency, disk usage, file permissions, and isolated test fixtures. Durable schemas remain unchanged. |
| Rollback path | Revert the scratch allocation and reaping change; no durable data migration is required. |

- Complexity: Medium (`tier:standard`)

- **Verification**: add SIGKILL aggregate and trim fixtures, dead-owner removal, live-owner preservation, unrelated-file and symlink preservation, legacy cleanup, concurrency, and permissions assertions. Baseline `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: 152 passed, 0 failed.

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Description

When all unresolved review threads on a PR are **positive observations** from `github-actions` or similar bots (comments that approve a change rather than requesting a fix), the review-thread-response worker exits with exit 0 without calling either `scanner.sh mark-complete` or `scanner.sh mark-blocked`. This violates the worker contract v2 and causes the scanner to retry indefinitely.

The scanner's permanent-skip gate (`_should_dispatch():891`) requires `analysis_complete=true && maintainer_attention=true`. Since the worker never calls a scanner state command, `analysis_complete` remains `false`, and the scanner dispatches a new worker every cooldown cycle (3600s) forever.

## Root Cause

**Worker behavior gap (Bug A):** The worker prompt instructs workers to call `mark-complete` or `mark-blocked` at step 5. For positive-observation threads ("this change is correct and more specific"), workers interpret the situation as "no action needed from me" and exit without:
1. Calling `scanner.sh resolve <thread_id>` (which would clear the thread)
2. Calling `scanner.sh mark-complete` (which would set `analysis_complete=true`)

The prompt does not explicitly say: *"even if all threads are positive bot observations approving the PR, you MUST resolve each thread and then call mark-complete."*

**Scanner lack of fallback (Bug B):** `_should_dispatch()` has no upper bound on retries when `analysis_complete=false`. After `ESCALATE_AFTER` (3) attempts it sets `maintainer_attention=true` but still dispatches new workers indefinitely because `analysis_complete=false` prevents the permanent-skip at line 891.

## Observed Evidence

**State file for PR #3071 in Majowka/mesh-manager:**

```
attempt_count=31         ← 31 hourly retries, all futile
worker_contract_version=2  ← current contract, not a stale-version issue
maintainer_attention=true
attention_reason=same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint
analysis_complete        ← ABSENT (never set)
```

**Scanner log** (`pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log`):

```
[2026-07-24T06:04:04Z] dispatch: Majowka/mesh-manager#3071 not launching response worker
  — same unresolved thread fingerprint reached attempt 30;
    maintainer attention recommended (local state/log only, no GitHub write)
[2026-07-24T07:12:18Z] dispatch: ...attempt 31; maintainer attention recommended
```

Cycle: `dispatched=1` → worker exits 0 → fingerprint unchanged → cooldown → retry.

**Thread content (all 24 threads on PR #3071):**

All from `github-actions`, all positive:
```
"The original code caught a generic Exception. This change updates the test to
 expect SQLAlchemyError, which is more specific and informative. This aligns
 with the principle of catching specific exceptions."
```

No code changes requested. Worker sees these, decides "no action needed", exits without resolving or calling mark-complete.

**Manual resolution** (interactive session):

if [[ "$state_repeated_same_fingerprint" == true
   && "$analysis_complete" == true        # ← NEVER set (worker doesn't call mark-*)
   && "$maintainer_attention" == true ]]; then

# Falls through to cooldown check → dispatches again

### Fix A — Worker prompt (primary)

Add explicit instruction for positive-observation threads. After the existing step 4 handling in the prompt template:

     verify the observation is accurate, then resolve immediately via
     `scanner.sh resolve`. Do not skip resolve for threads that require no code
     change — positive observations must still be resolved to satisfy branch
     protection.
```

And make step 5 unconditional:

```markdown

   outcome:
   - All actionable threads resolved: mark-complete
   - Any thread intentionally left unresolved: mark-blocked

   retry loops.
```

### Fix B — Scanner fallback (defense-in-depth)

```bash

# regardless of analysis_complete — catches workers that exit without

local absolute_cap=$(( PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_ESCALATE_AFTER * 5 ))

      "$state_repeated_same_fingerprint" == true &&
      "$state_same_head_sha" == true ]]; then

fi
```

body:
## Consolidation target: #28566

**Parent issue:** #28566 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** bug: worker-progress-blockers.jsonl never cleared for closed/not-planned issues — blocking=true persists forever, active blocker count inflated
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,triage-failed,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #28566. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references

   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #28566:**

```bash
gh issue comment 28566 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 28566 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 28566 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #28566 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

- **Do NOT read #28566** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Description

`worker-progress-blockers.jsonl` is an append-only log. Entries are written with `blocking: true` when a worker pauses for permission approval. The only path that writes `blocking: false` is `config-hook.mjs:355` — when a maintainer explicitly grants the permission and the worker resumes.

There is no path that writes `blocking: false` when:
1. The linked issue is closed or marked `not-planned`
2. The worker session exits for any reason without a grant
3. `sweep_closed_auto_dispatch_issues()` runs

**Result**: blocker records for closed issues accumulate permanently. `worker-activity-helper.sh` computes "active" blockers as the most recent event per identity with `blocking: true`. Once written, these records are never superseded.

## Observed Evidence

`worker-activity-helper.sh summary` reports `Currently active: 36`. Inspection of the actual issues:

| Session key | Issue | GitHub state | Blocker label | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `issue-3017` | #3017 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-2920` | #2920 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-1214` | #1214 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-2949` | #2949 Majowka/mesh-manager | **CLOSED not-planned** | none | 🪲 zombie |
| `issue-3088` | #3088 Majowka/mesh-manager | OPEN | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | ✅ legitimate |
| `issue-40` | #40 Majowka/aidevops-routines | OPEN | `needs-maintainer-permissions` | ✅ legitimate |

At least 4 of 6 visible "active" blockers are zombie records for closed issues. The 36 total likely contains many more.

## Causal Code

**`worker-blocker-log.mjs:83`** — default `blocking: true`:
```javascript
blocking: input.blocking !== false,  // only false when caller explicitly passes blocking:false
```

**`config-hook.mjs:354-355`** — the ONLY path writing `blocking: false`:
```javascript
recordPermissionGrantEvent({
    event: "permission_grant_applied",
    status: "resuming", reason: "scoped_permission_granted",
    blocking: false,   // ← only on successful grant
});
```

**`worker-activity-helper.sh:347`** — active = last event per identity with `blocking: true`:
```javascript
($all | group_by(identity) | map(sort_by(.ts // 0) | last)
      | map(select(.blocking == true))) as $active
```

**`shared-dispatch-label-cleanup.sh:123-130`** — `sweep_closed_auto_dispatch_issues()` strips GitHub labels only, never writes blocker events:
```bash
gh issue list --repo "$repo_slug" --state closed --label "auto-dispatch" ...
clear_terminal_issue_dispatch_labels "$issue_number" ...
# ← no appendWorkerBlockerEvent call here
```

## Proposed Fix

### Fix A — sweep writes unblock events (primary)

In `sweep_closed_auto_dispatch_issues()`, after clearing labels, write `blocking: false` events for any active blocker records matching the closed issue:

```bash
# After clear_terminal_issue_dispatch_labels:
node "${SCRIPT_DIR}/worker-blocker-log.mjs" append \
    --issue "$issue_number" --repo "$repo_slug" \
    --event "issue_closed_sweep" --status "resolved" \
    --reason "issue_closed_not_planned" --blocking false
```

### Fix B — worker-activity-helper cross-checks GitHub state (defense-in-depth)

When computing active blockers, skip identities where the linked issue is confirmed closed:

```javascript
# In _wah_blocker_json: filter $active against a small gh api batch
# to verify issue state — or at minimum add a TTL (e.g. 30 days)
```

### Fix C — TTL on blockers (simplest short-term)

Add a max age to "active" computation in `worker-activity-helper.sh`. Records older than 30 days are never counted as active regardless of `blocking` field.

## Workarounds Applied

None — the zombie records are cosmetic (inflated count, misleading diagnostics) but do not directly block dispatch. Legitimate blockers (#3088, #40) are still visible among the noise.

title: Defer queued dispatch ownership until pre-launch gates pass
body:
## What

Make queued dispatch ownership transactional at the worker-spawn boundary. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh::_dispatch_launch_worker`, defer the dispatcher assignee/status mutation and issue/linked-PR lock until the repeated-zero-output hold, worktree precreation, final worker-spawn gates, and prompt preparation have succeeded. Keep the existing exact-claim rollback for assignment or runtime-launch failures after ownership is acquired.

## Why

The current launch order assigns the dispatcher and applies `status:queued` before several expected pre-runtime aborts. The repeated-zero-output hold then removes `status:queued` and returns an abort. `_rollback_prelaunch_ownership` correctly refuses broad cleanup when queued ownership is no longer exact, so the dispatch claim is deleted while the dispatcher remains assigned. Worktree-precreation and final-gate failures also acquire and then roll back ownership unnecessarily.

This is the verified root defect behind PR #28237. That PR's broader unassign and historical-marker recovery paths weaken the exact-claim safety boundary; this maintainer-owned issue replaces that approach with a smaller launch-order fix.

## Evidence

Current order in `_dispatch_launch_worker`:

1. `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`
2. `_dlw_assign_and_label`
3. `_dlw_hold_repeated_zero_output`
4. `lock_issue_for_worker`
5. `_dlw_precreate_worktree`
6. `_dlw_final_worker_spawn_gates`
7. `_dlw_prepare_prompt_for_launch`
8. `_dlw_nohup_launch`

At `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh::_dlw_hold_repeated_zero_output`, the hold intentionally removes `status:available` and `status:queued` while adding `needs-maintainer-review`. At `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh::_rollback_prelaunch_ownership`, rollback only restores ownership when the exact current claim still owns both the dispatcher assignment and `status:queued`.

## How

### Files to Modify

title: bug: validate commit-and-pr metadata before branch mutation
body:
## Problem

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` validates explicit PR metadata while building the PR body, after staging, WIP-history finalization, project validators, rebase, and push. Invalid metadata can therefore publish a branch before the command reports an input error.

## Evidence

During PR #28580, invoking `commit-and-pr` with `--testing-level comprehensive` produced this order:

1. Finalized two WIP commits into one final commit.
2. Ran project validators successfully.
3. Rebasing completed.
4. Pushed `feature/auto-20260724-194143` to origin.
5. Exited with `Invalid --testing-level comprehensive. Expected runtime-verified or self-assessed.`

No PR existed after the failure, but the remote branch and rewritten commit had already been published. A second invocation with valid metadata was required.

## Implementation guidance

- In `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`, validate all explicit metadata options before `_stage_and_commit`, `_finalize_wip_history`, validators, rebase, or push.
- Reuse the accepted-value rules in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`; avoid duplicating divergent enums.
- Review both `--testing-level` and `--risk-level` for the same late-validation pattern.
- Keep derived defaults that require the final diff, but reject explicit invalid values before mutation.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh` or add a focused commit-and-PR ordering regression.

## Acceptance criteria

- Invalid `--testing-level` exits non-zero before any Git staging, commit rewrite, validator, rebase, push, or GitHub write.
- Invalid explicit `--risk-level` has the same fail-before-mutation behavior.
- Valid `runtime-verified` and `self-assessed` paths retain current PR-body output.
- A regression fixture records calls and proves that invalid metadata invokes none of the mutating helpers.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`
- Add and run the focused ordering regression if implemented separately.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`

# Phase 1 of #28587: Add corpus catalog and authorization foundations

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `knowledge corpus catalog workspace personal authorization resolver legacy personal alias Phase 1 aidevops` → 0 hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: current knowledge roots, modes, provisioning, add/list/search, workspace/RBAC guidance, and tenant-isolation patterns reviewed; no corpus catalog or knowledge-specific authorization resolver exists.
- [x] File refs verified: current entry points and tests listed below were read at `14a484f00`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — this leaf introduces a security-sensitive catalog schema and default-deny path resolver while preserving legacy storage behavior.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-25
- **Issue:** #28591
- **Parent:** #28587 / `t18176`
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive implementation
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Blocked by:** none; parent planning PRs #28588 and #28590 are merged.

## What

Implement the first independently mergeable social-knowledge foundation:

1. Add a private SQLite corpus catalog under the existing personal knowledge base.
2. Register the existing personal `_knowledge` tree as the `personal:default` alias without moving user files.
3. Derive the local principal from an owner-only authentication-context file rather than a caller-provided principal or corpus ID.
4. Resolve only active corpora granted to that principal through active workspace membership and explicit capability grants.
5. Keep existing `off`, `repo`, and `personal` modes and existing add/list/search behavior compatible.

This phase does not add social objects, archive/API ingestion, federated retrieval,
team key distribution, or browser capture; those remain in later parent phases.

## Why

The current personal mode directly opens one global path. Later personal/team
federation needs a physical corpus boundary and a default-deny resolver before
any social data is collected. The transition must be additive: existing users
keep the same personal path and no automatic file move occurs.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** SQLite schema invariants, authenticated-context handling,
filesystem permissions, cross-workspace isolation, and compatibility all need
joint reasoning and negative tests.

## PR Conventions

Use `Resolves #28591` for this leaf and `For #28587` for the parent. Do not close
the parent; successful merge should trigger Phase 2 auto-filing.

- **Stop when:** the catalog is idempotent, the legacy alias resolves through an authenticated grant, negative isolation tests pass, and repo/personal compatibility tests remain green.

2. Do not move ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/knowledge/_knowledge.
3. Store opaque IDs only in physical corpus paths and catalog primary keys.
4. Resolve identity from an owner-only local context file; never accept a principal ID as query input.
5. Require active principal + workspace + membership + corpus + capability grant.
6. Validate every resolved path remains inside the configured knowledge base.
7. Prove cross-workspace, forged alias, unsafe path, and bad context permissions fail closed.

1. Add bounded CLI, catalog, and context modules implementing schema-v1 initialization with the parent catalog tables, private alias indirection, WAL, foreign keys, busy timeout, atomic transactions, and `0600` database/context files beneath `0700` private directories.

3. Register `personal:default` with `location_ref=<personal-base>/_knowledge`; reject conflicting aliases or out-of-base locations.
4. Add list/resolve commands that derive the principal from the validated context file and require every active authorization edge before returning a path.
5. Wire personal provision/add/list/search to the helper while leaving repo mode untouched.
6. Add focused negative tests and run all existing knowledge compatibility suites.

- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Existing binaries ignore the new catalog and retain the legacy path; new binaries preserve `off|repo|personal` and the current personal location.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeated provisioning reuses the same principal/workspace/corpus and grants. A failed transaction cannot leave a partial authorization graph.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Missing, symlinked, wrong-owner, group/world-readable, malformed, or unknown-principal context fails closed. A catalog failure does not mutate legacy content.

title: fix(full-loop): avoid Critical runtime-risk false positives from documentation content
body:
## Problem

PR #28593 changed prompt/documentation surfaces and several runtime helpers. The first `commit-and-pr` attempt finalized and pushed the branch, then `_derive_runtime_risk()` classified the mixed diff as Critical because documentation text contained policy terms such as security, credentials, auth/session, and data deletion. Explicit Medium metadata cannot downgrade detected risk, so PR creation stopped until the already-executed helper tests were recorded as `runtime-verified` evidence.

The classifier treats the whole branch as non-Low when any runtime path is present, then concatenates the complete diff into one keyword context. Low-risk documentation and test hunks can therefore contaminate unrelated runtime classification. Derived risk is also enforced after push, allowing remote branch mutation before PR body generation is rejected.

## Evidence

- Observed in the interactive full loop for PR #28593.
- Original classifier implementation: PR #28469.
- Explicit-metadata pre-mutation validation: PR #28585.
- `_derive_runtime_risk()` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh` scans the unfiltered diff after `_runtime_paths_are_low()` fails for a mixed branch.
- `cmd_commit_and_pr()` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` pushes before `_build_pr_body()` derives and validates final risk evidence.

## Worker guidance

### Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`: make mixed-diff classification path-aware; exclude Low-only documentation, test, fixture, and linter-config hunks from runtime keyword detection while retaining summary and runtime-file evidence.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`: derive and validate final risk/testing evidence before remote push or GitHub mutation.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`: add mixed-path and mutation-order regression fixtures.

### Reference pattern

Preserve the conservative policy from PR #28469: explicit metadata may raise but never downgrade detected risk, and genuine Critical/High runtime changes require substantive `runtime-verified` evidence. Fix evidence attribution rather than weakening the gate or keyword set.

### Verification

- A harmless runtime-helper change plus documentation containing critical policy vocabulary does not become Critical solely from the documentation hunk.
- A real auth, credential, destructive-data, or other Critical runtime-code change still classifies Critical.
- Pure documentation/test/linter changes remain Low.
- Invalid derived risk/testing evidence blocks before push and GitHub writes; verify with mocked mutation counters.
- Run Bash syntax checks, ShellCheck, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.

title: bug: dependency reconciler rejects closed cross-repository blockers
body:
## Description

The dependency reconciler cannot release an issue that has a legitimate native cross-repository blocker, even when every blocker is positively closed.

In `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`, `_der_native_blockers_closed()` validates the `blockedBy` connection with:

```jq
.pageInfo.hasNextPage == false and all(.nodes[]; .repository.nameWithOwner == $repo)
```

This requires every blocker to belong to the dependent issue's repository. A native cross-repository blocker therefore makes reconciliation fail instead of allowing its `CLOSED` state to be evaluated. The stale sweep repeatedly counts these candidates as failures, leaving `status:blocked` in place after all dependencies close.

## Expected behavior

- Native blockers may belong to another repository when GraphQL returns their repository and state unambiguously.
- A dependent issue becomes `status:available` only when every native and declared blocker is positively closed.
- Open blockers, pagination, missing nodes, malformed data, inaccessible repositories, and API failures continue to fail closed.
- Existing human holds and active status labels remain untouched.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: update `_der_native_blockers_closed()` without weakening state or pagination validation.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: extend the existing same-repository, multi-blocker, ambiguity, and stale-sweep fixtures with cross-repository cases.
- Review merge/issue-close callers only to confirm they continue invoking the shared reconciler; avoid duplicating resolution logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- A candidate with closed same-repository and cross-repository native blockers is released.
- Any open cross-repository blocker keeps the candidate blocked.
- Inaccessible, absent, paginated, or malformed blocker data keeps the candidate blocked and returns a diagnostic failure.
- The event-driven close path and stale sweep produce the same result.
- Candidate discovery remains repository-bound; only blocker validation accepts cross-repository nodes.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- Run the repository's scoped ShellCheck/lint gate for the changed scripts.
- Add a regression fixture with one local closed blocker, one remote closed blocker, and one remote open blocker.
